_comment: Third-party repositories run_external.py scans -- Terraform and, since 2026-09-20, Kubernetes. `sha` pins the commit so a target cannot drift under its baseline; `baseline` is what the last --baseline run observed (absent until one has), and any later difference is reported as drift. `subdir` narrows the scan to one directory of the repo. Nothing here is vendored: the runner clones at run time into .repos/, which is gitignored.

repos.name: terragoat
repos.why: Vulnerable by design, and checkov's own. A volume and remediation-workload target, not a detection test: checkov will find its own cases.

repos.name: terraform-aws-vpc
repos.why: Well-maintained module with heavy variable indirection, for_each/dynamic blocks, and an examples/ tree of root modules. Parse robustness and false positives.

repos.name: terragrunt-infrastructure-live-example
repos.why: Terragrunt: .hcl wrappers over remote modules and no .tf at all. Documents what the scanner does with a repo shape it does not handle.

repos.name: kubernetes-goat
repos.why: Vulnerable by design, and the Kubernetes analogue of terragoat. A volume and remediation-workload target, not a detection test: its scenarios are written to be found.

repos.name: microservices-demo
repos.why: Google's Online Boutique: a well-maintained real application carrying plain manifests, a Helm chart, kustomize overlays, istio manifests, GitHub Actions workflows and GCP Terraform in one tree. The false-positive and repo-shape target -- and the only one where a single scan crosses two languages.

repos.name: argocd-example-apps
repos.why: The same guestbook app expressed eight ways -- plain, Helm, kustomize, jsonnet, sync hooks -- plus sock-shop. Documents what the scanner does with the packaging formats it does not handle, the way terragrunt does for Terraform.
